title: Canopy Light Mapping, Uniformity and Interlighting

content.overview: Average top-canopy PPFD can hide large differences among plant positions and canopy depths. Advanced lighting design measures distribution and uses fixture placement, canopy architecture or supplemental light to reduce harmful gradients.

vocabulary.definition: The degree to which light measurements are similar across a defined crop area.
Supplemental lighting placed within or beside the canopy rather than only above it.
A grid of measured photon flux values used to describe spatial distribution.

sections.title: A single PPFD value is not a light map
sections.body: Representative mapping uses repeated grid points and consistent sensor orientation. Minimum, maximum, average and variability all matter when judging canopy exposure.

sections.title: Architecture creates vertical gradients
sections.body: Upper leaves can intercept photons before they reach lower floral sites. Training, spacing and supplemental lighting can alter how light is distributed through the canopy.

sections.title: Interlighting can improve lower-canopy performance
sections.body: Recent commercial-scale research found interlighting could improve yield and chemical uniformity under the tested system, but economics and response remain facility-specific.

workedExamples: Two rooms with the same average top PPFD can differ if one has severe edge and lower-canopy deficits.
If interlighting improves lower-canopy uniformity but adds excessive heat or labor complexity, evaluate the whole production system rather than photon delivery alone.
commonMistakes: Measuring only at the center of the room.
Assuming higher average PPFD guarantees better uniformity.
content.practicalApplication: Create top- and mid-canopy PPFD grids, calculate range and uniformity, and compare them with flower position and quality data before changing fixture placement.
content.summary: Advanced light management is spatial. Mapping and uniformity reveal whether delivered photons reach the crop where they are needed.
